structured_output.review_summary: Static review of factory-receipt-discovery.py (1-827) and factory-receipts.py (1-294) only. I found three defects, two medium and one low. In discovery, a persisted backfill partition node can become permanently unloadable, a GitHub API failure during review source authentication aborts the whole review step, and the unfiltered discovery cursor revisits page 1 at exponentially growing intervals. I found no defects in factory-receipts.py. The strict source authentication, the nonforced PATCH CAS with lost-ack reconciliation, and the protected-origin and bootstrap-tree checks held up. Persisted facts do not grant coverage: coverage() re-observes the source listings and re-validates trust. A pass on those parts means only that this static read found nothing wrong.

findings.title: Count rising to >=1000 on a later page persists a split/gap node with an invalid page fact, wedging the campaign
findings.reason: Failure path: a partition node is in phase 'paging' with expected_count=500 and one retained page fact, and page 2 returns total_count>=1000 (for example, runs are still being created in the final interval second). The `elif count >= 1000` branch at line 322 runs before the count-drift branch at line 326. It sets facts=[fact] where fact['page']==query_page (2), page=2 and seen=this page's rows, then sets phase 'split' or 'gap'. The node is popped from the stack and persisted at part_path. On the next round the stored node is validated at lines 246-269 before the line-288 reset. The check at line 264-265 requires fact['page']==number (1), so it raises ValueError('backfill page facts malformed'). The part path is deterministic and only this function writes it, so every later backfill() call raises. coverage() at line 718 enforces the same check. The same corruption happens for lo==hi with reason 'dense-second'. Only a first-page (query_page==1) observation should be allowed to start a split. A later-page count rise should take the count-drift gap path, or the fact page should be normalized.

findings.title: GitHub API failures during source authentication or attempt fetch abort the review instead of classifying 'unavailable'
findings.reason: Elsewhere in this file a transient GitHub failure is a ValueError whose message starts with 'GitHub API request failed:'. Lines 155-158, 299-302, 524-526 and 824-825 map it to unavailable or a gap. The try block at lines 162-171 calls source_api.get for the attempt endpoint and source_fact, which calls api.source several times. Its `except ValueError` only maps messages containing 'not approved', 'source changed' or 'revoked', and re-raises everything else. A 404 or 5xx on the attempts endpoint, a missing runtime file at an old head_sha, or an oversize-source require() failure therefore propagates out of assess() and _checkpoint(). In review mode the cursor is only advanced after the loop and the checkpoint is committed after it, so a persistent failure on one watched row stops every later review invocation at that row. The GitHub-failure prefix should get the same handling as at line 155, and a missing-source failure should be classified 'unapproved' or 'unavailable'.

findings.title: Discovery cursor advances past the end of history and page 1 is revisited at exponentially growing intervals
findings.reason: In discover mode next_page is set to page+1 unconditionally, even when the page is empty (line 562). The overlap schedule (lines 473-478) resets overlap_until to page-1 each time a cycle completes, so the cycle length roughly doubles each round. Tracing from (overlap, until)=(1,1) gives page-1 refetches at calls 2, 3, 4, 6, 10, 18, and so on. After the listing is exhausted, every call fetches an empty page plus one overlap page and commits a progress-only commit. Runs newly created at the head of the unfiltered listing are first observed only when the overlap cursor reaches page 1, at geometrically growing delay. next_page also grows toward the 10**9 validation bound at line 39. The cursor needs a wrap-around to page 1 when a page comes back short or empty. Interval coverage from backfill is not affected, because backfill adds the missing watch rows.

limitations: Static review of the supplied text only. I did not run anything. This is not native provenance or operational acceptance.

Dependencies were not reviewed: factory-receipt-archive.py (verify_bootstrap, retained_execution, append_delivery, reconstruct_interval, fixed_reader, document and canonical), factory-state-paths.py, coordinator.require, and the api.source and api.request implementations. I assumed that require() raises ValueError and that GitHub transport failures raise ValueError('GitHub API request failed: ...'), as lines 155-156 and 300-301 imply. If require() raised RuntimeError, the handlers at lines 166, 191 and 823 would classify validation failures as unavailable.

Sections A, B and D, including the project_reporting path called from factory-receipts.py:235, were out of scope. I made no judgment on the stage acknowledgement, journal CAS, PR discovery, or driver and workflow requirements.
Delivery behavior of the coordinator's merged=false receipt format was not visible, so I could not check validate_shadow's required eligible=True against the real producer.
I did not form any view on whether the 1001-run cadence, Slack delivery or activation work.
